title: Build a month-end close checklist agent
description: A system that tracks your month-end close checklist against target dates and flags what's overdue or blocked, grouped by owner.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

slack.title: Slack
slack.content: The team messaging app most companies run on. In Level 2, students connect Slack to their AI tools to trigger workflows from messages, post AI-generated updates to channels, or summarize threads automatically.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

notion.title: Notion
notion.content: An all-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project tracking. Used heavily across the AI Builder program as a destination for AI-generated content and as a connected app in Level 2 automations.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

children.text: Close speed splits on process discipline. Top-quartile organizations close their books in 4.8 calendar days or fewer, the median sits at 6.4 days, and the bottom quartile takes 10 or more, per [APQC's cycle time research](https://www.apqc.org/resource-library/resource/cycle-time-perform-monthly-close). This system tracks your close checklist against target dates and task order, flags anything overdue or blocked, and groups the picture by owner so nothing surfaces for the first time on the last day of close.

It doesn't do the accounting judgment. It matches reported status against the checklist, catches what's late or waiting on a prerequisite, and nags on it before it becomes the reason close slips another day.

Run it as a paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) at the start of each close cycle, a saved skill your team runs daily through close, or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that checks in each morning and posts to [Slack](#tooltip-slack).

Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming your checklist tasks and owners, what counts as overdue or blocked, and how status updates reach the agent.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that walks my team through month-end close and nags on overdue tasks. Ask me questions, one at a time, about what's on my current close checklist, what order tasks need to happen in, who owns each task, how I want overdue items flagged, and what "done" looks like for each step. Then write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview forces you to define "done" and "overdue" before you build, so the first cycle doesn't start with a false alarm.

items: Where your close checklist lives today, before you can automate tracking it.
How task status updates reach the agent, since someone still has to report done.
Who gets the overdue nag and how often, so it helps instead of becoming noise.

children.text: Bring the scope document. Pressure-test it first by pasting it into a fresh session or a different [model](#tooltip-model) and asking it to poke holes. Then gather what it calls for: a task or project tool for the checklist itself ([Notion](#tooltip-notion), Asana, Trello), your accounting system for task-relevant data (QuickBooks, NetSuite), and Slack for reminders and status updates. The paste-in version needs none.
**Create.** Build and test the system on the current close cycle, with the latest status attached. The prompt below is one example; your scope document has the full version.

children.prompt:
Goal: Track our month-end close checklist and tell me what's overdue or blocked right now.

Context: Our close checklist: [paste the full list of tasks, owners, and target dates]. Today's date and where we are in the close cycle: [day X of close]. Status update from the team: [paste any Slack/email updates on what's done].

Rules: Match reported status against the checklist and target dates. Flag anything past its target date as overdue, and anything whose prerequisite task isn't done yet as blocked. Never mark a task complete unless someone explicitly reported it done. Group output by owner so each person sees only their items first, then show the full picture.

Output format: A status table (Task, Owner, Target Date, Status: done/overdue/blocked/on-track), followed by a short list of what needs attention today.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: explicit rules for overdue and blocked keep the output consistent from day to day instead of a guess about what needs attention.

children.text: **Review.** Check the output against your checklist. Every owner's items accurate, blocked tasks tied to a real prerequisite, nothing marked done without a report?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly what's wrong (a task wasn't really blocked, an owner's grouping is off) and fold each correction into the rules.

items: Add a rolling history so you can see which tasks are chronically late and why.
Connect it to your accounting system to auto-check tasks like bank reconciliation instead of relying on manual reporting.
Build a post-close retro that summarizes what slowed this cycle down.
Extend the same pattern to quarterly or annual close.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric) instead of a feel check. Have your AI chat draft rubric and run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each close status report, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for close date, tasks flagged overdue, flags that turned out to be real, false positives, and what rule I changed. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks remove the judgment call, and the log columns make recurring misfires visible after a cycle or two.

children.text: **Log** every run. Note the date, which rubric checks passed or failed, and what changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an instruction you haven't written yet.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the rubric passes a few cycles straight, package the prompt and corrected rules into a skill, so every run starts from your defaults. A repeated failure earns its own skill. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s skill-creator skill will interview you and write it, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).

One durable failure mode. A checklist agent that lets a task get marked done without real confirmation just moves the risk of a missed step later and hides it better, so status updates need a real, verified source behind every "done."

items: [APQC, Cycle Time to Perform the Monthly Close](https://www.apqc.org/resource-library/resource/cycle-time-perform-monthly-close) — Close cycle time benchmarks by performance quartile.
